config.title: Pagination

intro.title: Pagination
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple pagination component for a list of items. You will learn how to split a large dataset into smaller, manageable pages and navigate between them. The core concepts include using React state to track the current page and calculating which items to display. You will work with JavaScript arrays for slicing data and React JSX to render the page numbers and content. This hands-on project will help you understand how to handle data display in user-friendly chunks.
intro.usecase: Pagination is essential for managing large datasets in real-world applications like e-commerce product listings, search engine results, and content management dashboards. Developers implement pagination controls in product catalogs, admin panels displaying user records, and social media feeds to improve performance and user experience. This pattern appears in data tables, blog archives, and API-driven applications where limiting displayed items prevents overwhelming users and reduces load times. Mastering pagination enables building scalable interfaces that handle growing data while maintaining responsive navigation.

objectives: Initialize React state to track the current page and total items for pagination
Implement a function to calculate the total number of pages based on items per page
Construct a component that renders pagination controls with previous/next buttons
Configure event handlers to update the current page when users click pagination buttons
Manipulate array data to display only the items for the current page
Integrate pagination logic with a list component to display paginated content
Render dynamic page number buttons that update based on the current page range

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the Pagination component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Pagination that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to export the component.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the Pagination component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named Pagination is defined and exported, returning an empty div.
successCriteria: The component is named Pagination, returns a div element, and is exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Pagination component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Pagination, returns a div, and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check the name, return value, and export.

steps.title: Initialize current page state
steps.instruction: Inside your Pagination component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'currentPage' with an initial value of 1.
steps.hint: Call useState(1) and destructure the returned array into two variables: currentPage and setCurrentPage.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a counter
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'currentPage' initialized to 1, ready to track the active page.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call with initial value 1, destructured into currentPage and setCurrentPage variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an initial value of 1, and destructuring it into two variables: currentPage and setCurrentPage.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization isn't quite right. Remember to use useState(1) inside the component and destructure the result.

steps.title: Initialize total pages state
steps.instruction: Inside your Pagination component, add a second useState hook to initialize a state variable named 'totalPages' with a default value of 10.
steps.hint: Call useState(10) and destructure the returned array into a variable named totalPages and its setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a second state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: currentPage and totalPages, both managed with useState.
successCriteria: A state variable named totalPages is declared with useState, initialized to 10.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable named totalPages with an initial value of 10.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Remember to add a second useState call inside the component to create a totalPages state variable initialized to 10.

steps.title: Create goToNextPage handler
steps.instruction: Inside your Pagination component, define a function named goToNextPage that increments currentPage only if currentPage is less than totalPages.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses setCurrentPage to update the state. You can check if currentPage < totalPages before incrementing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The goToNextPage function should be defined inside the component and conditionally increment currentPage.
successCriteria: A function named goToNextPage is defined that increments currentPage only when currentPage < totalPages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it checks if currentPage is less than totalPages before incrementing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The goToNextPage function is not defined correctly. It should increment currentPage only when not on the last page.

steps.title: Add pagination container
steps.instruction: Return a div element with className 'pagination' as the main container for your pagination controls.
steps.hint:
Replace the current return statement (return null) with return (
).
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div with className 'pagination' as its structure.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element with className 'pagination'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div element with className 'pagination'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div with className 'pagination' as its structure.

steps.title: Add previous button and wire click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the Pagination component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Previous' and wire its onClick event to the goToPrevPage handler.
steps.hint: Add <button onClick={goToPrevPage}>Previous</button> inside the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Previous' button appears in the pagination UI that will trigger navigation when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element with text 'Previous' and onClick handler calling goToPrevPage is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the button has both the text 'Previous' and the onClick handler set to goToPrevPage.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly configured. Check that you've added <button onClick={goToPrevPage}>Previous</button> inside the return statement.

steps.title: Add current page display
steps.instruction: Add a span element inside the pagination container that displays the current page number and total pages. The text should show 'Page {currentPage} of {totalPages}'.
steps.hint: Use a span element with the text content that includes the currentPage and totalPages variables. Place it between the previous button and any upcoming next button.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying dynamic values in a span Score: {score} / {maxScore}
steps.expectedOutcome: The pagination UI now shows the current page number and total pages in a span element between the previous button and any upcoming next button.
successCriteria: A span element is added that displays 'Page {currentPage} of {totalPages}' using the currentPage and totalPages variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a span element, but it doesn't display the current page and total pages correctly. Make sure to use the currentPage and totalPages variables in the text content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The current page display is missing or incorrect. Add a span element that shows 'Page {currentPage} of {totalPages}' using the currentPage and totalPages variables.

steps.title: Add next button and wire click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Next' and wire its onClick event to the goToNextPage handler inside your Pagination component.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element after the current page display. Set its text content to 'Next' and use onClick={goToNextPage} to connect it to your handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Next' button appears in the pagination UI that will advance to the next page when clicked.
successCriteria: The component contains a button with text 'Next' and an onClick attribute set to goToNextPage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a button with the exact text 'Next' and connected it to the goToNextPage handler using onClick.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Next button isn't properly implemented. Check that you've added a button element with text 'Next' and onClick={goToNextPage}.
